key_insight: Dynamic masking lets particle-tracking data be reconstructed on a grid while enforcing moving solid boundaries, yielding boundary-consistent, divergence-free velocities near bodies.
engineering_relevance: This improves pressure and hydrodynamic force estimation in volumetric PTV for flows with translating, rotating, or deforming solids.
method: Use a time-dependent signed-distance field to label fluid, boundary shell, and solid regions.
Solve Lagrangian-to-Eulerian reconstruction with incompressibility and prescribed surface velocity on the masked domain.
Apply the same framework to stationary, moving, multiple, or deforming bodies with only a signed-distance field and surface velocity.
evidence_signal: Validated on an analytical oscillating sphere, synthetic CFD rising-sphere tracks, and a tomographic-PTV freely rising sphere experiment, with first-cell error reduced from 14% to 3% of body speed in the analytical case.
watch_item: Performance depends on an accurate signed-distance field and prescribed surface velocity; errors in either can degrade boundary enforcement near the body.
paper_title: Dynamic masking for boundary-aware velocity reconstruction in volumetric particle tracking with moving solids
